meta.subtitle: IoT and Edge AI hardware maker turning toward unmanned-systems compute; FY26 revenue $120.9M, net cash balance sheet, still GAAP loss-making.

analystCommentary: Lantronix rates a BUY with a target range of $8.00 to $11.00, against a current price of $6.25 and a probability-weighted fair value of $8.55. The call rests on a business in transition. FY26 revenue was $120.9M, {- -1.6% -} lower, yet the company closed the year on what management called its fifth consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth, with Q4'26 revenue of $31.2M. Gross margin improved again in FY26. The company is still GAAP loss-making: FY26 net income was -$4.2M and diluted EPS was $-0.10, though that loss narrowed from $-0.29 in FY25. The balance sheet is the anchor, with about $60 million of cash and no debt, a current ratio of 3.66, and free cash flow of $9.3M at a 7.7% FCF margin. The forward case leans on unmanned systems, which contributed $12.6M of FY26 revenue and which management guides to 15% to 20% of total revenue in FY2027, and on double-digit growth guidance; consensus models higher FY27 revenue and positive EPS on its estimates, a basis the pack does not label, set against the FY26 GAAP loss. Six analysts rate the stock Buy with a $10.25 consensus target. The bear case is real: revenue fell 23.3% in FY25, the company depends on a small number of distributors and customers, and its unmanned-systems growth is tied to defense and government budgets the filing flags as uncertain.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Lantronix, Inc., incorporated in 1989 and headquartered in Irvine, California, develops and sells industrial and enterprise Internet of Things (IoT) products and services across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and the Asia Pacific Japan region. Management organizes the portfolio into three product lines: Embedded IoT Solutions, IoT Systems Solutions, and Software and Services. Embedded solutions include compute system-on-module and system-in-package products, plus application processing for data transformation, computer vision, and machine learning. IoT Systems Solutions cover routing, switching and gateway functions, telematics, media conversion, and wired and wireless connectivity, including power over Ethernet and out-of-band management. The company positions itself as a provider of Edge AI and Industrial IoT solutions for NDAA-compliant unmanned systems, critical infrastructure, and enterprise networks. It manages its sales teams by three geographic regions, the Americas, EMEA, and APJ, and reports as a single reportable segment; the filing gives no product or geographic revenue split, so FY26 revenue of $120.9M is shown as one consolidated line. Substantially all manufacturing is outsourced to contract manufacturers in Asia.

thesis.body: The investment case is a turnaround priced with option value. FY26 revenue of $120.9M was down 1.6%, but that followed a {- -23.3% -} decline in FY25, and the company closed FY26 with its fifth consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth. Gross margin improved year over year, and the FY26 GAAP loss of $-0.10 per share narrowed from $-0.29 in FY25. The new growth engine is unmanned systems, which contributed $12.6M in FY26 from a minimal base and which management expects to reach 15% to 20% of FY2027 revenue. With about $60 million of cash, no debt, and $9.3M of free cash flow, the company can fund this shift and the Nero Global Tracking acquisition without leverage. The counter-case is that FY26 revenue still fell, the company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis, and the growth thesis leans on defense and government demand that the filing itself flags as uncertain.

catalysts: Management guides to double-digit revenue growth in FY2027; the underlying consensus revenue and EPS estimates are carried in the valuation and financials sections.
Unmanned systems, established as a growth engine in FY26, is guided to represent a materially larger share of total revenue in FY2027.

The August 2026 acquisition of Vecima Networks' industrial IoT business and its Nero Global Tracking SaaS platform adds recurring, subscription-style revenue, with the economics set out in the growth section.

A March 2026 U.S. Court of International Trade ruling may entitle the company to refunds of IEEPA-based tariffs it has paid, though the timing and amount remain uncertain and none has been recognized.
Addition to the Russell 3000 Index in the 2026 reconstitution broadens the shareholder base.
risks: The company depends on a small number of distributors and end-user customers, so the loss of one or a decline in their orders could materially cut sales.
Unmanned-systems growth is tied to U.S. and allied defense and government budgets, which the filing notes can be cut, delayed, or terminated for convenience.
Some integrated circuits are single-sourced and the market is experiencing memory shortages, exposing gross margin to component cost and availability.
FY26 revenue still declined year over year and the company remained GAAP loss-making with a net loss of $4.2M, so the growth inflection is not yet proven in the full-year numbers.
Substantially all manufacturing is outsourced to contract manufacturers in Asia, with no guaranteed supply agreements.

financials.incomeCommentary: FY26 revenue was $120.9M, down 1.6%, the second straight annual decline after FY25 fell {- -23.3% -} and FY24 rose {+ +22.2% +}. Gross margin improved to 43.8% in FY26 from 42.1% in FY25 and stands above each of the prior four years, at 42.9%, 42.9%, 40.1%, and 42.1%. Operating margin was -3.4% in FY26, better than -8.9% in FY25 but still negative, and the company has run an operating loss in each of the last five fiscal years. GAAP diluted EPS was $-0.10 in FY26, narrower than the $-0.29 loss in FY25; net income was -$4.2M. On a non-GAAP basis the company reported EPS of $0.15 for FY26 and $0.04 for the fourth quarter. Q4'26 revenue was $31.2M, up 4.6% year over year on the desk's figures; the company's press release described the same quarter as up 8%, and we use the 4.6% figure. The fourth-quarter operating margin was -1.3%. Consensus models revenue of $138.6M in FY27E and $157.2M in FY28E, with EPS estimates of $0.23 and $0.32; the pack does not label those estimates GAAP or non-GAAP, so we read them as positive forward EPS set against the FY26 GAAP loss rather than as a confirmed GAAP profit, especially since the company already prints positive non-GAAP EPS.
financials.balanceCommentary: Lantronix ended FY26 with about $60 million in cash and no debt, a net cash position the desk records as net debt of -$60.5M; total debt was zero. The current ratio rose to 3.66 at FY26 from 2.54 a year earlier and is the strongest in the five-year series of 2.53, 2.08, 2.95, 2.54, and 3.66. Management described the year-end balance sheet as the strongest in the company's history. The company carries goodwill tied to a single reporting unit; its qualitative assessment in the fourth quarter of FY26 did not indicate impairment, so no quantitative test was required. Deferred tax assets are fully offset by a valuation allowance, reflecting historical net operating losses and uncertainty about future taxable income. The clean, net-cash balance sheet gives the company room to fund the Nero Global Tracking acquisition, which closed on August 1, 2026, from existing resources.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Free cash flow was $9.3M in FY26, a 7.7% FCF margin, and positive for a third straight year after FCF margins of 10.7% in FY24 and 5.5% in FY25; the two earliest years of the window were negative, at -8.9% and -1.9%. Capital expenditure was light at about $612,000 in FY26, consistent with an outsourced-manufacturing model that keeps the asset base thin. Positive free cash flow alongside a GAAP net loss reflects non-cash charges; the company's non-GAAP reconciliation adds back share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, and amortization of purchased intangibles, among other items. Cash generation at this level comfortably covers the modest capex program and leaves the net cash balance intact.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: On trailing earnings the stock has no meaningful multiple: P/E is -62.5x because the company is loss-making, and EV/EBITDA is not defined. Price-to-sales is 2.4x on FY26 revenue. The forward multiples price in the expected earnings recovery: the next-twelve-months P/E is 27.0x, and the forward P/E on the FY28E earnings estimate is about 19.5x. The peer column is blank pending a peer data source, so these are company-only figures. The Street is uniformly positive: six analysts rate the stock Buy, none at Hold or Sell, with a consensus target of $10.25, a median of $10.50, and a range of $8.00 to $12.00. Our target range sits inside the Street range and brackets our $9.00 base case, and the probability-weighted fair value of $8.55 stands above the current $6.25.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Unmanned systems scales to the upper end of the FY2027 revenue share management targets, double-digit growth carries the top line past the FY27E consensus, and positive forward EPS earns a re-rating toward the top of the Street's $12.00 target.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Revenue grows toward the FY27E consensus, the Street's positive EPS estimates hold, and the stock re-rates into the lower half of the Street target range on modest multiple expansion from the current 2.4x sales.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Customer concentration, component shortages, or defense-budget timing stall the recovery; revenue stays near FY26's $120.9M, GAAP losses persist, and the multiple compresses, taking the stock about 20% below the current $6.25 to $5.00.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: The three scenarios weight to a fair value of $8.55, above the $6.25 current price, with the Base case at $9.00 carrying a 45% probability. The Bull case at $12.00 (25%) assumes unmanned systems and the Nero acquisition drive double-digit growth and positive forward EPS on the Street's estimates, matching the top of the Street's target range. The Bear case at $5.00 (30%) is a genuine downside: it sits about 20% below the current price and reflects the risks the filing names, from dependence on a few large customers to single-sourced components, memory shortages, and defense demand that can be cut or delayed. The spread between Bull and Bear is wide because the company is at an inflection: FY26 revenue still declined 1.6% and the GAAP result was a loss, so the market is paying for a recovery the full-year numbers have not yet delivered. We skew the reward to the upside but retain that Bear weight on the case where the turn does not arrive.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Lantronix reports as a single reportable segment, so FY26 revenue of $120.9M appears as one consolidated line with no product or geographic split disclosed. Within that segment the company organizes its offerings into three product lines: Embedded IoT Solutions, IoT Systems Solutions, and Software and Services. Management frames the business around three strategic focus areas: unmanned systems, critical infrastructure, and enterprise networking. Consolidated gross margin is covered in the financials section, and the recurring Software and Services mix in the growth section.

moatFactors.name: Embedded design-in stickiness
moatFactors.body: Embedded system-on-module and system-in-package products are designed into customer platforms, which can raise switching costs once a customer qualifies a component. The same filing notes reliance on a small number of customers, so any benefit is concentrated rather than broad.

moatFactors.name: Certification and compliance barriers
moatFactors.body: The company emphasizes NDAA-compliant unmanned-systems compute and pre-certified products; certification and compliance requirements can narrow the field of qualified suppliers for defense and critical-infrastructure buyers. This edge is early and not yet visible in the financials.

moatFactors.name: Pricing power
moatFactors.body: Five consecutive years of operating losses and a stated risk of intense competition and resultant downward price pressure indicate the company does not yet command pricing power. Gross margin improved in FY26, as the financials section details, but the operating line stayed negative.

moatFactors.name: Scale
moatFactors.body: At its FY26 revenue level the company is small relative to the markets it targets, and it outsources substantially all manufacturing, which limits cost advantages from scale.

businessMoat.durability: The evidence does not yet support a durable economic moat. The company has posted operating losses in each of the last five fiscal years, and a risk factor cites intense competition and resultant downward price pressure. What could build durability over time is the shift toward unmanned-systems compute and critical infrastructure, where NDAA compliance, certifications, and embedded design-ins raise the bar for competitors, and toward recurring Software and Services revenue that the Nero acquisition is expected to expand, as detailed in the growth section. Until margins turn positive and revenue growth is sustained, the moat is best treated as prospective rather than realized. The improved gross margin and a net cash balance sheet give the company time to prove the thesis.

points: Consensus models double-digit FY27 revenue growth, rising further in FY28E, consistent with the estimates carried in the financials section.

Unmanned systems grew to $12.6M in FY26 from a minimal base and are guided to 15% to 20% of total revenue in FY2027, with active engagements expanded to more than 30 at year-end from about 10 at the start of FY26.
Partnerships with Swarmer, DoD Solution, and AVT Australia extend the company's system-on-module and compute platforms into drone and autonomy programs.

The Nero Global Tracking acquisition adds about $5.3 million of annual revenue, including roughly $4.5 million of ARR and about 125,000 asset tags under management, and lifts recurring Software and Services above 10% of revenue on a pro forma basis.
The SLC 9000 out-of-band console manager, integrated with Percepxion, targets the AI data center networking market.
The company guides Q1 FY2027 revenue of $31.0 million to $33.0 million.

management.leadership: Saleel Awsare is president and chief executive officer and a director. In the FY26 results release he framed the year as one of measurable progress, citing a return of the core business to growth, a stronger balance sheet, and the establishment of unmanned systems as a growth engine. The proxy lists a board that includes James Auker, Sailesh Chittipeddi, and Hoshi Printer as directors, with Narbeh Derhacobian and Kevin Palatnik as director nominees, alongside executives Mathi Gurusamy, Chief Product and Strategy Officer, and Kurt Hoff, Chief Revenue Officer. The five-year record is mixed: revenue grew 22.2% in FY24, then fell 23.3% in FY25 and 1.6% in FY26, and the company has not produced a GAAP profit over that span.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital allocation has favored balance-sheet strength and targeted M&A over shareholder returns. The company returns no cash to shareholders: no dividend, and no buybacks across the five-year window. It ended FY26 with net cash and no debt, and it deployed roughly $11.7 million in August 2026 to acquire Vecima Networks' industrial IoT business and the Nero Global Tracking SaaS platform, whose revenue and ARR contribution is set out in the growth section. Capital expenditure is light, reflecting outsourced manufacturing, and positive free cash flow funds this approach internally without drawing on debt.
management.governance: Governance disclosures rest on the DEF 14A proxy statement filed on September 24, 2025. The proxy reports no transactions with related persons that required disclosure during fiscal 2025 or fiscal 2024. The company indemnifies its directors and officers to the fullest extent permitted by law and has entered into indemnification agreements with each of them. The proxy's beneficial-ownership table is measured against 39,271,361 shares outstanding as of September 8, 2025; the current share count is higher, at about 46.71M, so ownership percentages drawn from the proxy predate more recent issuance. The proxy excerpt does not carry full board-independence or compensation detail, so this section does not opine beyond what is disclosed.
management.insiderOwnership: Insider and large-holder ownership is concentrated among a few names. As of September 8, 2025, Bernhard Bruscha held 13.8% (5,423,357 shares, largely through TL Investment GmbH) and Chain of Lakes Group held 7.8% (3,072,343 shares), the two holders above 5%. President and CEO Saleel Awsare held 1.1% (447,960 shares). All current executive officers and directors as a group, nine persons, held 2.4% (951,464 shares). The modest insider stake means management's alignment comes more through compensation than through a large founder-sized equity position.

idiosyncratic: Customer concentration: the company has historically relied on a small number of distributors and end-user customers for a significant portion of net revenue, and the loss of one, or a decline in their orders, could materially reduce sales and raise excess inventory.

Government and defense exposure: growth in drone and defense markets depends on customers winning government contracts, which are subject to congressional appropriations, budget cuts, shutdowns, and termination for convenience, making the timing of these sales unpredictable.

Supply chain and components: some integrated circuits are single-sourced or no longer manufactured, the market is currently experiencing memory shortages that raise costs, and the company has at times been unable to fill orders for lack of components; it holds no long-term supply agreements with most vendors.

Execution on the pivot: FY26 revenue still fell 1.6% and the company remained GAAP loss-making, so the shift to unmanned systems and higher-margin software must scale before it shows up in full-year profitability, and integrating the Nero Global Tracking acquisition adds execution risk.

Tariff and trade uncertainty: the company has paid IEEPA-based tariffs and, following a March 2026 U.S. Court of International Trade ruling, any refund is uncertain in timing and amount, while future trade-policy and tariff changes could raise costs.
risks.systemic: Systemic risks sit largely outside the company's control. The filing cites worsening regional and global economic conditions and their effect on customer purchasing decisions, changes in U.S. trade policy and tariffs, and conflicts in Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, including hostilities in the Red Sea and tensions between China and Taiwan, as factors that could disrupt supply chains and demand. Rising interest rates and the stability of financial and banking institutions are also named. Because substantially all manufacturing is outsourced to contract manufacturers in Asia, the company is exposed to regional disruption and trade friction there. As a small-cap with a $291.9M market capitalization and a 52-week range of $4.37 to $8.75, the stock is more volatile than the broad market and more sensitive to shifts in risk appetite for unprofitable growth names.

body: We rate Lantronix a BUY with a target range of $8.00 to $11.00 against a $6.25 price, below the Street's $10.25 consensus but above the current quote. The call is a turnaround with option value: FY26 revenue of $120.9M was still down 1.6% and the company remained GAAP loss-making at $-0.10 per share, but gross margin improved year over year, free cash flow was positive, and the balance sheet holds about $60 million of cash and no debt. The recovery hinges on unmanned systems, guided to 15% to 20% of FY2027 revenue, and on the double-digit growth management expects, which consensus reflects in higher FY27 revenue and positive EPS estimates whose basis the pack does not label.

The probability-weighted fair value is $8.55, with a 45% weight on the $9.00 base case and a real 30% weight on a $5.00 bear that sits about 20% below the current price. We would turn more constructive as sustained revenue growth and positive earnings arrive, and more cautious if customer concentration, component shortages, or defense-budget timing stall the top line. Six analysts currently rate the stock Buy, with none at Hold or Sell.
